title: Baffin's autograph map of his fourth voyage to the north-west, 1615
creator: William Baffin
description: Facsimile of the manuscript chart William Baffin drew of the 1615 voyage in the Discovery with Robert Bylot, from British Museum Add. MSS. 12206. The coasts Baffin himself saw are washed in colour, the ship's track is pricked in red, and the unseen shores are left as faint outline - an honest map of what was and was not observed. It covers Hudson Strait, Foxe Channel and the approaches to Southampton Island.

title: Baffin's Bay on five successive charts
creator: Markham (ed.)
description: A fold-out plate setting five charts of Baffin Bay side by side, from Baffin's own delineation of 1616 through the eighteenth-century blanks to the nineteenth-century surveys - the plate Markham used to argue that Baffin's much-doubted bay had been right all along.

title: Entrance to the Persian Gulf, to illustrate the last voyage of Baffin
creator: Markham (ed.)
description: Chart of the entrance to the Persian Gulf, showing Qeshm and Ormuz, where Baffin was killed in January 1622 while taking the height of a wall under fire during the East India Company's siege - the end of the navigator who had charted Baffin Bay six years earlier.

title: Baffin's journal table of the 1615 voyage, page 106
creator: William Baffin
description: The first of five ruled table pages in which Baffin set out the 1615 voyage day by day: the date, the latitude, the variation of the compass, and a remarks column. This page carries the departure and the passage from Padstow.

title: Baffin's journal table of the 1615 voyage, page 107
creator: William Baffin
description: Table page recording the working through the ice towards the island of Resolution at the eastern mouth of Hudson Strait, with the daily latitude and the compass variation.

title: Baffin's journal table of the 1615 voyage, page 108
creator: William Baffin
description: Table page for the passage through Hudson Strait past the Savage Islands, with a note of eight days' stay and a longitude reckoned five degrees west from London - among the earliest longitude estimates from these waters.

title: Baffin's journal table of the 1615 voyage, page 109
creator: William Baffin
description: Table page for the western end of the strait: Cape Comfort, Nottingham and Salisbury islands, the north shore within Resolution Island, and the ice the Discovery worked through.

title: Baffin's journal table of the 1615 voyage, page 110
creator: William Baffin
description: The last of the table pages, running home past Cape Farewell, with Baffin's own bracketed note on the reverse of the conjecture.
